title: United Airlines 2860
summary: United Airlines Flight 2860, a DC-8 cargo flight, departed San Francisco on December 17, 1977, with an intermediate stop planned at Salt Lake City. After reporting electrical trouble during descent, the crew entered a holding pattern and left the frequency to discuss the problem with maintenance. Unaware of the incomplete holding clearance, the flight drifted into mountainous terrain. When ATC warned of terrain and ordered an immediate climb, the aircraft struck a 7,665-foot mountain ridge at 7,200 feet, killing all three crew members.
probable_cause: The National Transportation Safety Board determined the cause was the approach controller's issuance of an incomplete and ambiguous holding clearance, combined with the flightcrew's acceptance of it and failure to follow prescribed loss-of-communications procedures and holding procedures. The controller and crew's actions were attributed to habitual imprecise communication and adherence developed through years of radar environment operations. Contributing to the accident was the aircraft's No. 1 electrical system failure.

factors.evidence: The approach controller issued an incomplete holding clearance without specifying a holding radial (p. 33-34)
The flightcrew failed to adhere to prescribed loss-of-communications and holding procedures (p. 33-34)
Due to incomplete clearance and crew workload, the aircraft entered a hazardous area of terrain while off frequency (p. 34-35)
Aircraft impacted 7,665-foot mountain ridge at 7,200-foot elevation (p. 3)

events.text: United Airlines Flight 2860 departed San Francisco at 2317 PST on December 17, 1977
Flight began descent from cruise altitude toward Salt Lake City
Crew reported electrical trouble and requested holding clearance
Crew requested to leave frequency for 'little minute' to contact United maintenance
Controller approved crew to leave frequency, believing it would be brief
Flight returned to approach control frequency
Controller warned flight of terrain on right and instructed left turn
Controller instructed climb immediately to 8,000 feet
Crew reported climbing from 6,000 feet to 8,000 feet
Aircraft struck 7,665-foot mountain ridge at approximately 7,200 feet elevation

recommendations.text: Review the adequacy of current cockpit voice recorder preflight testing procedures to assure satisfactory system operation
Review the reliability of cockpit voice recorder units to assure that the mean time between failure is not excessive
